nodes.description: the code the change lives in
why the surrounding code is as it is
who last touched a line, and when

edges.guidance: Call git_diff first. Every judgement in this review is about what the diff changed, so reading anything else before it is reading without a question.
edges.pitfalls: Do not begin by listing directories or grepping. You do not yet know what you are looking for.

edges.condition: a changed file contains code the diff does not show in full
edges.guidance: Read each changed file once, in as few calls as the 300-line cap allows, starting at the first changed hunk. The diff shows the change; the file shows what the change is embedded in, and correctness is a property of the second.
edges.pitfalls: Never re-read a range you have already read. Every earlier read is still in this conversation above you — scroll rather than call. Reading one file in a series of overlapping windows is the single most common way a review runs out of budget with nothing submitted.

edges.condition: the change claims something about a test, a build or a lint that a command can settle
edges.guidance: Run the allowlisted command and attach its real output. A finding backed by a failing command outranks ten arguments.
edges.pitfalls: Only the exact allowlisted strings run; a near miss is refused, not approximated. If no command is allowlisted, reason from the code and say so rather than retrying.

edges.condition: the change alters something other code depends on - a signature, a constant, a schema, an error shape
edges.guidance: Grep once for the specific symbol. What you are looking for is a caller the change breaks, or an existing implementation the change duplicates.
edges.pitfalls: Do not re-issue a pattern you have already run. If a pattern returned nothing, a slightly reworded version of it will also return nothing; the answer is that the thing is not there.

edges.condition: reading the code produced a suspicion a command could confirm
edges.guidance: Confirm it before reporting it. An unconfirmed suspicion belongs in the finding's confidence, not in its title.

edges.condition: you have read the changed code and nothing specific is still in question
edges.guidance: Submit. Fewer well-supported findings is the expected outcome, and an empty list is a real result.
edges.pitfalls: Do not keep reading in the hope that something turns up. If you cannot name the question the next call answers, you are finished.

edges.condition: a hit is in a file you have not read
edges.guidance: Read the hit and the lines immediately around it, by line range. You want the one call site, not the file it lives in.
edges.pitfalls: Do not read the whole file for one hit, and do not read a file you have already read.

edges.condition: the search answered the question, either way
edges.guidance: A search that found nothing is an answer. Record what it settled and move on.
History explains intent; it rarely produces a finding on its own. Return to the diff or submit.

edges.condition: blame points at a change you have not read

edges.guidance: You now know the layout. Search it for the thing you were looking for rather than listing further.
edges.pitfalls: Listing a directory you have already listed tells you nothing new. Two listings of the same path in one review is a sign of being lost — go back to the diff.

edges.guidance: Attach the command's real output as the finding's evidence, including the exit code.
edges.pitfalls: If the command failed for an environmental reason rather than because of the change, say so and do not report it as a defect.
